Key Fukuoka Areas
Where Fukuoka’s Audiences Are

Fukuoka’s audiences are concentrated in a handful of walkable districts and transport hubs. The right mix depends on the objective, the dates and the screens available through participating media partners.
Tenjin

Fukuoka’s main shopping, office and entertainment district, with department stores, an underground shopping street and substantial pedestrian activity. The Tenjin Big Bang redevelopment is introducing new office and retail spaces, creating opportunities for brands to connect with shoppers, professionals and younger consumers.
Hakata Station
The city’s rail hub and the southern end of the San’yo Shinkansen, combining commuters, business travellers and shoppers in the station complex and surrounding offices.
Fukuoka Airport

Unusually close to the city centre and linked by subway, so arriving domestic and international travellers move quickly into Hakata and Tenjin. In 2025 it handled 8% of Japan’s international air passengers.
Hakata Port and Bayside
Japan’s leading port for foreign cruise calls in 2024, plus ferry connections with Korea, bringing international visitors into the city on arrival days.
Canal City Hakata and Nakasu
Shopping, entertainment and Fukuoka’s best-known nightlife and food-stall area, busy with visitors in the evening.
Momochi and Seaside
Home to Fukuoka Tower, Mizuho PayPay Dome Fukuoka and waterfront retail, with large crowds on game and event days.

Buying Fukuoka DOOH: Direct, Programmatic or Both

For regional agencies and media owners, demonstrating campaign value to advertisers increasingly requires more than traditional site-based media planning. As digital advertising acquisition costs rise, DOOH offers an opportunity to build physical brand exposure and connect it with subsequent digital engagement.

Some Fukuoka briefs need a fixed presence at Hakata Station or in Tenjin for a set period; others need flexible delivery that follows visitors and shoppers across the city. Direct activation secures specific sites, while programmatic DOOH uses defined budgets, dayparts, audience signals and impression-based buying to support more flexible campaign delivery.

For D2C and e-commerce brands, this creates an opportunity to use DOOH as an upper-funnel channel that builds awareness and supports subsequent digital interactions, rather than relying exclusively on digital acquisition channels.

Moving Walls technology powers MASTRUM, the impression-based DOOH platform launched with JR East Marketing & Communications (jeki), whose first phase brought about 34,000 screens across Japan onto one system. Which Fukuoka screens are available programmatically depends on the media owners and integrations available for your campaign.
